cover.title: Fabulous Frogs
cover.subtitle: A Hop into the World of Frogs

pages.text: Frogs are amphibians. That means they can live in water and on land! Frogs have been around for a very, very long time -- even longer than dinosaurs.
extras: There are over 7,700 kinds of frogs!

images.alt: A European common frog sitting on a mossy surface

pages.text: Frogs have smooth, wet skin that helps them breathe. They have big eyes on top of their heads so they can see in almost every direction. And their long, sticky tongue can catch a bug faster than you can blink!
extras: The smallest frog is as tiny as your fingernail.
The biggest frog weighs as much as a baby!

images.alt: A bright green European tree frog clinging to a stem

pages.text: Frogs live all over the world -- except Antarctica! Many frogs live near ponds, rivers, and swamps. Some live high up in rainforest trees and never come down to the ground.
extras: Wood frogs can freeze solid in winter and hop away in spring!

images.alt: An Australian green tree frog sitting calmly on a branch
A wood frog sitting on leaf litter on the forest floor

pages.text: Frogs love to eat bugs! Flies, mosquitoes, and crickets are all yummy frog food. A frog catches its dinner with a long, sticky tongue -- snap! It is so fast you would miss it if you blinked.

images.alt: An agile frog in profile showing its long hind legs

pages.text: Frogs lay their eggs in water. The eggs look like a squishy blob of jelly called frogspawn. Baby frogs are called tadpoles. They have long tails and no legs, and they eat tiny plants in the water.

images.alt: Close-up of frogspawn showing round eggs in clear jelly
Tadpoles eating together in shallow water

pages.text: As a tadpole grows, something amazing happens. It sprouts legs! Its tail gets shorter and shorter. Soon it looks just like a frog. This big change is called metamorphosis.
extras: It can take weeks or even months!

images.alt: A tadpole with legs growing and its tail shrinking during metamorphosis

pages.text: Frogs are amazing jumpers! Their strong back legs help them leap really far. Tree frogs have sticky pads on their toes that work like suction cups to help them climb.
extras: Some frogs can glide through the air!

images.alt: A small frog caught mid-jump with powerful back legs extended
Close-up of a frog's webbed foot showing skin between its toes

pages.text: There are so many cool frogs! Poison dart frogs are tiny with bright colors that say "stay away!" Flying frogs spread their big webbed feet and glide from tree to tree.

images.alt: A bright red strawberry poison dart frog on the forest floor
A flying frog with large webbed feet spread out for gliding between trees

pages.text: Frogs have clever ways to stay safe. Some blend in with leaves and mud so other animals cannot see them. Frogs sing loud songs to find their friends. Frogs help us too -- they eat lots of pesky mosquitoes!
extras: Every kind of frog has its own special song.

images.alt: A northern leopard frog with a spotted pattern that helps it blend in
A green tree frog with its vocal sac inflated, calling loudly
